sourceBehavior: Initial roster and later updates use identical presence handling: JOINING, JOINED and ACTIVE create or retain a participant; DISCONNECTED removes it.
nativeBug: Initial roster accepted only ACTIVE, while later updates accepted every non-DISCONNECTED value. The same JOINED participant could therefore unblock client warmup only if a later update happened to arrive.
fix: Both native paths now share membership handling for explicit known JOINING, JOINED and ACTIVE states; DISCONNECTED removes peers. Empty, self and unknown-state participants cannot authorize startup.
securityBoundary: Roster presence starts media/QUIC negotiation only. It does not grant mutual authentication or proxy access; pinned certificate checks are unchanged.
causality: This corrects a source-proven order-dependent startup bug. Whether it resolves the production subscriber timeout requires the next controlled test.
independentRuledOutHypothesis: A real local application-only subscriber offer connected ICE/DTLS without a local data channel; no production datachannel workaround was added.
tests: Initial roster and update parity across all four known states, duplicate suppression, self/empty/unknown rejection.
Initial JOINED participant unblocks actual LkTunnel startup without setting peerAuthenticated.
